findings.text: follow-on: robustness - the fold pattern _SEPARATED_CELSIUS_RE = r'\bdeg\.\s*C\b' requires the period, so a space-only spelling 'deg C' is not folded and still resolves to 'C.deg' (degree times coulomb, a current-times-time dimensionality). Reproduced at head: normalize_unit_symbol('deg C') == 'C.deg' while normalize_unit_symbol('deg. C') == 'degC'. The catalogue corpus carries only the period-bearing 'deg. C', so this is latent rather than a live defect, and the source comment accurately states the period is required. Fix if wanted: make the corpus sweep cover 'deg C', or widen the pattern to r'\bdeg\.?\s+C\b' with a test.

follow_ons: none blocking. (1) The reviewed run's own manifest after_suite.revision reads c38e99b9772c8a8f1341c4622444e8b9425c4422 while the log it cites (gate_head_degc.log) was regenerated at the final head 66cdc2c16; the log itself is at 66cdc2c1 and is valid, only the manifest's revision label is stale - a provenance labelling slip, outside this review's commit scope. (2) The prior review's two findings are both closed by this commit: the fragment intro no longer claims a glued form is an @alias, and 'deg. C' no longer resolves to a coulomb-dimensioned unit.

justifications.durability: 18: the guard test_dd_unit_normalisation_is_not_regressed now asserts the moved set equals INTENTIONAL_CORRECTIONS exactly, so a future unintended unit change still fails. Deducted because the fold regex requires the period, leaving a latent space-only 'deg C' mis-resolution uncovered and untested (see findings).
justifications.evidence: 19: I ran independent base (a8998c5a, 891 passed) and head (66cdc2c1, 892 passed) arms in scratch trees extracted with git archive, plus my own negative control that removes the preprocessor registration and the early fold and shows exactly test_separated_celsius_spelling_is_a_temperature and test_dd_unit_normalisation_is_not_regressed fail (2 failed, 394 passed, EXIT=1). The fragment's census numbers reconcile with census.json.
justifications.fit: 19: the fold uses the registry-preprocessor mechanism pint already offers, and the fragment and source comments explain why a name-level @alias cannot carry the spelling, consistent with the module's existing idiom.
justifications.goal_fidelity: 19: the commit resolves the exact defect the plan names - the catalogue's 'deg. C' free-text spelling resolved to a coulomb-dimensioned unit - by folding it onto the degC alias, and it refuses to guess the equally-cased 'V.S' rather than emit a current-dimensioned reading. Both were the prior review's open findings and both are closed here.
justifications.reuse: 18: one helper _fold_separated_celsius is used at two call sites (the preprocessor and the early fold before the canonical vocabulary), which the run's own manifest records as one function rather than two mechanisms. Deducted one because the canonical authority runs in its own registry, so the same fold is applied twice on the single path.
justifications.scope_discipline: 20: the commit touches only the units module, its evidence fragment and its tests; no unrelated files, no graph write.
